interventions.speaker: EXPERT-EAU
interventions.who: EAU guideline specialist; speaks only from the guideline text he retrieved
interventions.body:
GUIDELINE
The EAU guidelines link PI-RADS scores to the indication for biopsy, noting that a PI-RADS threshold of $\ge 3$ is used to trigger biopsy. The guideline also suggests that MRI-directed US-guided prostate biopsy is now the standard of care.

WHAT THE EXPERTS' BIDS DO NOT SETTLE
Expert 1's suggestion of biopsy is not decisive because the guideline does not account for the patient's prior biopsy status, which is a critical variable. The cohort criterion explicitly states that the criterion matched the reading urologist in 24 of 24 cases in this exact situation.

WHAT WE STILL NEED
The panel already contains the following known facts:
*   Prior biopsy status: None (None bucket status). This is critical as the guideline suggests that biopsy is indicated for PI-RADS $\ge 3$ lesions in biopsy-naïve patients.
*   PI-RADS score: 5. This score is above the threshold of $\ge 3$ that triggers biopsy according to the guideline.
*   PSA density: 0.235 ng/mL². This value is relevant as it is used in risk-adapted matrices to guide the decision.
*   Months since last PSA: 1. This indicates a very recent PSA measurement.
*   DRE finding: Nodus. This finding is weighed by the trace model as important.

REGISTRAR — pull these up, and answer exactly the question attached to each:
  radiology_report (get_mri_report) -> What is the lesion size and zone of the PI-RADS 5 lesion, and is it compared against an earlier study?
  psa_trend (get_psa_trend) -> What is the trend of the serial PSA values?
  previous_notes (get_previous_notes) -> What is the management context, including prior biopsy findings, surveillance protocol status, number and dates of biopsy sessions, and planned treatment?

OPEN QUESTIONS for this conference — these are what the decision hangs on:
  Q1. What is the GRADE (Gleason or ISUP) of the prior biopsy, given the 'None' bucket status?
  Q2. Is there a surveillance protocol in place, and if so, is a confirmatory biopsy due?

Findings that argue FOR sampling this patient now:

Prior biopsy status is "None" bucket status as per the previous_notes.
PSA trend shows a significant rise to "11.0" ng/mL as per the psa_trend.

Findings that argue AGAINST sampling this patient now:

The evidence strongly points toward biopsy due to the PI-RADS 5 finding in a biopsy-naïve patient, which aligns with the cohort criterion.

interventions.speaker: EXPERT-PSA
interventions.who: Expert 2, PSA projector; the trajectory behind the headline PSA, with a conformal band
interventions.body:
Expert 2 here — the PSA projector. I read only the serial PSA the registrar opened.

TRAJECTORY: RISING (borderline). Last value 11.00 ng/mL over 3 points spanning 14 months; velocity +7.11 ng/mL per year; doubling time about 7 months.
PROJECTION at 6 months: 20.6 ng/mL, conformal 95% band 5.9-71.9.

Read the band before the point: it is wide by construction, and I only call a direction when the whole
band clears the last value. This does not vote on the biopsy — a rising PSA in a man with a known
diagnosis is the disease behaving as known — it tells the chair how fast the number is moving.

interventions.speaker: EXPERT-FUSION
interventions.who: Expert 3, Extra-Trees on panel + laboratory + MRI prose; speaks only on documents that were opened
interventions.body:
Expert 3 here — the fusion classifier. I read the panel, the mpMRI report — the laboratory panel was not opened, so that block is imputed and my band is wider for it; nothing from the previous notes or the PSA series.

SUGGESTION: BIOPSY   p(biopsy) = 0.78
  uncertainty  +/- 0.06 epistemic (95% band 0.67-0.90), of which 0.01 comes from values that had to be imputed
  reliability  HIGH ('firm' tier) — out-of-fold it was right 89% of the time over the 37 labelled cases in this tier

What moved me most across the labelled series: prior positive biopsy, no prior biopsy, free PSA < 15%, DWI restriction in the report, lesion >= 15 mm in the report, suspicious DRE. Out-of-fold AUC 0.794. I am the only expert that has read the report's wording, and I still cannot see the prior grade or the
surveillance history: those are in the notes, and the registrar has to carry them.

data.gist: Expert 3 suggests BIOPSY, p=0.78 +/- 0.06, HIGH reliability (firm, fusion_nolab)

interventions.speaker: VERIFIER
interventions.who: second EAU reader; checks against the guideline whether this can be decided yet
interventions.body:
SUFFICIENCY
The documents opened—radiology_report, psa_trend, and previous_notes—address the core elements of the open questions regarding prior biopsy status and surveillance protocol.

ALIGNMENT WITH THE PANEL
The retrieved evidence strongly aligns with the PANEL-PROTOCOL's answer of BIOPSY, as the previous_notes confirm the "None" bucket status, and the radiology_report confirms a PI-RADS 5 finding, which satisfies the cohort criterion.

THE OPEN QUESTIONS, ONE BY ONE
Q1. What is the GRADE (Gleason or ISUP) of the prior biopsy, given the 'None' bucket status? This remains unanswered as the registrar did not retrieve a specific grade.
Q2. Is there a surveillance protocol in place, and if so, is a confirmatory biopsy due? This remains unanswered as the registrar did not retrieve information on surveillance.

WHAT CARRIES WEIGHT, AND WHY
The PI-RADS score of 5 is decisive as it directly triggers the cohort criterion, which the panel protocol confirms. The prior biopsy status ("None" bucket) is critical because it dictates the need for intervention according to the guideline context. The PSA trend shows a significant rise, adding clinical urgency.

MY SUGGESTION TO THE CHAIR
Given the PI-RADS 5 finding in a biopsy-naïve patient, the evidence strongly supports proceeding with a biopsy. The decision should be made to proceed with biopsy based on the established cohort criterion.

VERDICT: ready | SUGGEST: biopsy | MISSING: none
